english: Let $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ be a differentiable function such that $f(-2)=1$ and $y=f(x)$ satisfies the differential equation $2\left(x^{2}+4x+13\right)\dfrac{dy}{dx}=3\left(y^{2}-2y+2\right)$ for all $x\in\mathbb{R}$. Then the value of $f(2)$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ एक अवकलनीय फलन है जिसके लिए $f(-2)=1$ है तथा $y=f(x)$ सभी $x\in\mathbb{R}$ के लिए अवकल समीकरण $2\left(x^{2}+4x+13\right)\dfrac{dy}{dx}=3\left(y^{2}-2y+2\right)$ को सन्तुष्ट करता है। तब $f(2)$ का मान ______ है।
solution_full: At $x=-2$, $y=1$: $0=0+C$, so $C=0$. The right side lies in $\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{4},\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)$, so $y=1+\tan\left(\dfrac12\tan^{-1}\dfrac{x+2}{3}\right)$ is defined for all $x$.
originality_note: New: a separable equation with a quadratic on each side whose two arctan coefficients stand in the ratio 1:2, so the value needs the half-angle of tan^-1(4/3) and comes out rational (way 5). Closest known: separable DEs dy/(1+y^2) = dx/(1+x^2) giving tan^-1 y = tan^-1 x + C. Different because: the two sides have different scales, the relation is a half-angle, and the evaluation uses tan(phi/2) = sin(phi)/(1+cos(phi)).
key_step: Completing both squares, integrating to tan^-1(y-1) = (1/2) tan^-1((x+2)/3), and a half-angle evaluation.
justification: Routine chain of standard results (separation, two standard integrals, half-angle) with no hidden idea. Level 2 like 2026-P2-Q3 (L2) separable DE with a non-trivial finish.
blueprint_concepts: Integrals of the form int dx/(ax^2+bx+c) and int dx/sqrt(ax^2+bx+c)

concept_use.Integrals of the form int dx/(ax^2+bx+c): Both sides are integrals of the form dx/(ax^2+bx+c) with negative discriminant, giving tan^-1 terms after completing the square.
concept_use.Variable separable equations: The equation separates as dy/((y-1)^2+1) = (3/2) dx/((x+2)^2+9), and f(-2) = 1 fixes the constant.
